datasets: 311 Customer Service Requests 2026 (GeoJSON, 812 MB, submitted separately)
Neighborhood Statistical Area (NSA) Boundaries (GeoJSON, 279 polygons, submitted separately)
concurrency_primitives: two loader goroutines + sync.WaitGroup (cmd/engine/main.go:30-34); worker-pool point-in-polygon join over bounded jobs/results channels with context cancellation and WaitGroup-closed results (internal/processing/joiner.go:46-92); segmented parallel aggregation with per-goroutine maps merged via channel (internal/analysis/analyzer.go:56-111)
design_patterns: Pipeline (load -> spatial join -> analyze -> report) across internal packages; fan-out/fan-in worker pool; no Strategy/Factory interfaces
questions: Which neighborhoods report the most problems?
What problems are most common in each neighborhood?
Where is the highest percentage of problems still unresolved?
Where does it take the longest to fix problems?
Which neighborhoods need the most attention? (40% volume + 40% unresolved rate + 20% mean closure time)
overview: Idiomatic multi-package Go (cmd/engine + internal/ingestion, processing, analysis, output, models) with tests in every stage package. Loads both GeoJSONs concurrently, assigns 311 points to NSA polygons with a bounded worker pool (ray casting with holes, bbox prefilter), aggregates in parallel segments, and prints five ranked tables with # bars. Compact and readable, but the loader reads and unmarshals the whole 812 MB file at once.
stakeholder_value: On the real data it produces plausible, cross-validated rankings (Belair-Edison 24.8k requests, campus neighborhoods with the highest open rates, Curtis Bay Industrial 25-day closures). However every question is a 311-only statistic; the boundary dataset merely supplies a grouping key the 311 file already has, and the NSA layer's population/vacancy attributes go unused, so there is no genuine cross-dataset insight and stakeholders are not named.
issues: All five questions are single-dataset 311 aggregates; NSA boundaries used only as a spatial lookup key; no named stakeholders.
Entire 812 MB GeoJSON read with os.ReadFile and fully unmarshalled: 2.26 GB RSS, no streaming decoder.
Synthetic sample GeoJSON is the default flag path (rubric -3); real data was uploaded separately and had to be symlinked into data/ per README.
Parsing is not parallel (one goroutine per file); ~235k null-geometry 311 records dropped without being reported.
run-windows.cmd contains leftover text referencing 'the old project'.
Race detector not run on the full dataset (memory risk); clean on tests and sample.
rationale: Full marks for build, run and README, and near-full for architecture, because the program is cleanly packaged, tested, and completes on the real 700k-record dataset in 20 seconds. Deductions: memory 5/10 for the read-all loader, real_data 12/15 for the synthetic default path, concurrency 12/15 because parsing is not parallel, and stakeholder 7/15 because the questions never combine attributes from both datasets. Total 80 (B).
